_comment: The field-level delta between what Orrery emits and what the published
profile defines, both directions, every field classified.
VERDICTS for a field Orrery emits:
MAPPED                 -> the profile defines it (possibly under another
name). `protocol` must be a property of the
published schema.
DRIFT                  -> the profile SHOULD carry it and does not. This is
a HARD FAILURE, not a note: a DRIFT entry fails
the suite until the profile is moved forward.
The list is empty by construction.
DELIBERATE-EXCLUSION   -> stays out of the envelope on purpose.
WHY DELIBERATE-EXCLUSION IS NOT A LABEL THAT EXEMPTS. Each entry is a claim
the suite checks against both sides:
* the field must actually be emitted by Orrery  -> no phantom exclusions
* every emitted field must appear here exactly once -> nothing opts out by
being unlisted
* the field must be ABSENT from the published schema -> the moment the
profile adopts it, the exclusion becomes false and this suite goes red.
That is the cross-repo drift detector: it fires on a change made in the
OTHER repository.
* `reason_code` must be one of the closed set below and `reason` must be a
real justification, not a restatement of the field name.
reason_code:
PROFILE_FORBIDS        -> §3 forbids this content class. `reason` must cite
the section.
OUT_OF_PROFILE_SCOPE   -> the profile has no such concept; adding one is a
protocol decision, not this suite's to make.
IMPLEMENTATION_INTERNAL-> an artifact of how Orrery computes intelligence,
meaningless to a peer that computes it otherwise.

fields.reason: Renamed by genericization. 'chapter' is NANDA-specific vocabulary; the published profile federates 'communities'. Same value, same meaning.
Renamed by genericization, as chapter_id -> community_id. Same value, same meaning.
Identical shape and meaning: {skill: integer weight} over the whole community.
Identical: the list of skills the community lacks, as plain strings.
Identical: the list of topics gaining attention, as plain strings.
Identical: list of strings. Note Orrery emits this key only when its intelligence cache is populated; the empty-cache branch omits it. Both branches are classified here.
Identical: highest-weighted skills derived from skill_graph, capped at ten on both sides.
Identical: the aggregate count of members, carrying no per-member identity.

Was the one real DRIFT this measurement found: Orrery emitted it and the published envelope had no property for it, so with additionalProperties:false the signal could not be carried at all. Resolved by moving the PROFILE forward (sm-federation 0.3.0) rather than by making Orrery drop it — it is an aggregate count with no per-member identity, the same class as member_count, so §3 permits it. Orrery derives it as len(intel['active_members']); 'active_members' itself is a member LIST and is never emitted (see the note in protocol_only).

Free-text behavioural patterns named by Orrery's own reflect cycle ('weekly cadence', ...). They describe how Orrery models its members, not a fact about the community, and a peer running a different intelligence model cannot interpret them. Exporting them would put one implementation's internals into a vendor-neutral wire format.

When Orrery's reflect cycle last rebuilt its intelligence model. Deliberately NOT mapped to the profile's generated_at, which is when the SNAPSHOT was produced — a different fact. Mapping them would make a stale snapshot look fresh, or a fresh snapshot of a stale model look stale. generated_at is caller-supplied at envelope build time.

Rows of Orrery's federated governance policy, shipped to peers for the cross-chapter policy merge. Federated policy is an entire subsystem with its own trust model and merge semantics; the published profile has no concept of it and giving it one is a protocol decision, not something a conformance suite should infer from one implementation.

protocol_only.reason: The sm-feed payload discriminator. Orrery has no feed transport at all, so nothing consumes a discriminator. Required by the profile — this is part of why the intelligence-envelope-emitter claim is implemented:false.
Orrery's summary carries no envelope version, so a peer cannot tell which profile produced it. Required by the profile.

Orrery stamps fetched_at on the RECEIVING side instead, so the timestamp reflects when the reader pulled, not when the sender snapshotted — a clock the sender does not control and cannot be held to. Required by the profile.

not_emitted_by_either.reason: Reported upstream as an emitted field; it is not. It is an INPUT key inside Orrery's intelligence cache (a list of member identifiers), read by get_our_summary only as len(...) and by two local A2UI surfaces. It never reaches the federation wire, and it must not: §3 forbids per-member identifiers in an envelope. Recorded here so the claim is not re-litigated, and asserted by the suite so it stays true.
